land.text: New Sweden on the Delaware: Fort Christina and the settlements 'on both sides of the Delaware River'

successors.note: 'New Sweden was conquered by the Dutch Republic in 1655 and incorporated into the Dutch colony of New Netherland' (New Sweden page); Fort Christina surrendered on 15 September 1655.

capitals.name: Fort Christina (Wilmington, Delaware)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Fort Christina' without dates; the Fort Christina page calls it 'the principal settlement of the New Sweden colony'. Governor Printz had his manor house, the Printzhof, at Fort Nya Gothenborg on Tinicum Island (about 1643-1653), which the page does not call a capital. Coordinates are the editor's, for Wilmington's Rocks.

rulers.name: Peter Minuit
rulers.title: Governor
rulers.note: Died in a hurricane at St. Christopher on a later voyage; Captain Måns Nilsson Kling then carried out the governor's duties (New Sweden page).

correction.text: Fort Christina and the Delaware's west bank down to Delaware Bay that Minuit bought from the Lenape in 1638; the colony is not on the east bank until Fort Nya Elfsborg (1643)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first New Sweden shape begins in 1640 but the Swedes landed on 29 March 1638 ('The Swedes' arrival is dated on March 29, 1638') and built Fort Christina, 'the principal settlement of the New Sweden colony'. Only the west-bank core is drawn until the 1643 east-bank fort.

2,841 km2 along both banks of the Delaware around Wilmington (bbox 39.26-39.97 N, 75.86-75.12 W). The page gives no area figure to compare with, but names the settlements: 'Settlements were established on both sides of the Delaware River' and the Swedes claimed land 'from the Schuylkill River down to Delaware Bay'. The east-bank part is not Swedish before Fort Nya Elfsborg (1643) and the Fort Casimir cells are Dutch from 1651 to May 1654, but the shape stands as the best single outline of the colony at its yearly resolution.

correction.text: The same Delaware shape as Cliopatria draws, valid only 1653 to September 1655; Cliopatria keeps it to 1658 but 'New Sweden was conquered by the Dutch Republic in 1655 and incorporated into the Dutch colony of New Netherland', so 1656-1658 belong to New Netherland

keyframe_review.note: Years only: shape unchanged, ends 15 September 1655 (the surrender of Fort Christina). The shape includes Fort Casimir (New Castle), which the Dutch built in 1651 and the Swedes held from May 1654 to summer 1655. The page gives no area, so the 2,841 km2 could not be compared with an infobox figure.

region.text: Fort Christina at 'The Rocks', about 1 mile east of present downtown Wilmington, Delaware, and the west bank bought from the Lenape in 1638

ledger.note: 1638: the Swedes land at The Rocks on the Christina River and build Fort Christina. 'The Swedes' arrival is dated on March 29, 1638' under Peter Minuit; the fort is 'the principal settlement of the New Sweden colony'. The New Sweden page (a second page for this event) says Minuit 'persuaded the Lenape to sign deeds' in 1638 for land on the west bank, and the Swedes claimed land 'from the Schuylkill River down to Delaware Bay', which the Lenape sachem Mattahoon later disputed as covering only land within 'six trees'. Region is the west-bank part of Cliopatria's 1640 shape, my reading; no page gives a boundary.

region.text: the east bank of the Delaware around Fort Nya Elfsborg, near Bridgeport, New Jersey

ledger.note: 1643: Fort Nya Elfsborg is built on the Delaware's east bank. The page lists 'Fort Nya Elfsborg (1643), near Bridgeport, New Jersey' and says 'Settlements were established on both sides of the Delaware River'; other posts: Upland (Chester, 1641 and 1643), Fort Nya Gothenborg on Tinicum Island (1643), Fort Nya Vasa (1646) and Fort Nya Korsholm (1647). Region is the New Jersey part of Cliopatria's 1640 shape, my reading.

region.text: Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity), on the west bank of the Delaware at present New Castle

ledger.note: 1654 (May): New Sweden strikes at the Dutch. 'In May 1654, soldiers from New Sweden led by Governor Johan Risingh captured Fort Casimir and renamed it Fort Trinity' (Trefaldigheten); the Dutch had built the fort in 1651 after abandoning Fort Nassau.

region.text: Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity), on the west bank of the Delaware at present New Castle

ledger.note: 1654 (May): Fort Casimir falls to the Swedes under Johan Risingh and is renamed Fort Trinity.

region.text: Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity), on the west bank of the Delaware at present New Castle

ledger.note: 1655 (summer): Stuyvesant retakes Fort Casimir. His forces 'quickly retook Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity)' before besieging Fort Christina; the page gives no day.

region.text: the lower Delaware, the Swedish settlements and Fort Casimir

ledger.note: 1655 (15 September): the Delaware fighting ends. Fort Christina 'surrendered on September 15, 1655' after Stuyvesant's siege (the Fort Christina page: 'after ten days').

region.text: New Sweden on the Delaware: Fort Christina and the settlements 'on both sides of the Delaware River'

ledger.note: 1655 (15 September): Fort Christina surrenders and New Sweden is lost to the Dutch. 'New Sweden was conquered by the Dutch Republic in 1655 and incorporated into the Dutch colony of New Netherland'; settlers kept their militia, religion, court and lands, and Fort Christina was renamed Fort Altena.

region.text: the whole colony, to New Netherland

ledger.note: 1655: New Sweden ends. Its land passes to New Netherland, which the English take in 1664 (the page: the Dutch period 'lasted until the English conquest of New Netherland in 1664'); the 1669 Revolt of the Long Swede, which tried to restore Swedish rule, failed.

wars.name: Dutch-Swedish conflict on the Delaware (1654-1655)

zones.text: Fort Casimir (Fort Trinity) and the lower Delaware

wars.outcome: Dutch victory: the Swedes took Fort Casimir in May 1654; Stuyvesant retook it in summer 1655 and Fort Christina surrendered on 15 September 1655, ending New Sweden.
wars.note: The New Sweden article carries the campaign inside its own sections; no separate war page was opened (page budget). The Dutch dossier new-netherland records the same fighting from its side.

certainty.note: Settlements along the Delaware, no survey: the Swedish claim 'from the Schuylkill River down to Delaware Bay' rests on a 1638 Lenape deed the Lenape later said covered only land within 'six trees'; the Dutch claimed the whole river, so the Fort Casimir area is a contested edge throughout.

sources.title: New Sweden
sources.note: Identity, 1638-1655, forts and settlements, claims, the 1654 and 1655 fighting, governors.

sources.title: Fort Christina

notes: Cliopatria's New Sweden is 1640-1658 (two identical 2,841 km2 shapes); the colony lasted 1638 (landing 29 March) to 15 September 1655, so a core keyframe is added for 1638-1639 and the 1653 shape is cut at 1655 (1656-1658 are New Netherland, whose dossier new-netherland already holds the matching Fort Casimir and Fort Christina events). Neither page gives an area. The map outline is one block along both banks; the east bank only becomes Swedish with Fort Elfsborg in 1643 (ledger). Month of the founding is the landing date, 29 March 1638; the Fort Christina page does not give the construction month. Coordinates for the capital and the Fort Casimir radius are the editor's. Pages opened: 2 of a budget of 1-2. The Lenape (counterpart 'nobody' in the 1638 and 1643 gains) have no Cliopatria row; if am-05 writes a Lenape dossier the counterpart can be changed.
